name: Error Squelch
description: Suppresses Drupal status, warning, and error messages whose text matches configured patterns (substring or regex).

suggests.drush/drush: Enables drush error-squelch:list/add/remove commands for managing patterns from the CLI.

project_description:
Suppresses Drupal status, warning, and error messages whose text matches an admin-configured list of patterns, so known-benign notices stop cluttering screenshots, training videos, client demos, and on-call dashboards while a proper fix is pending. Suppression is purely cosmetic and does not address the underlying condition that produced the message.

How it works: the OO hook implementation Drupal\error_squelch\Hook\ErrorSquelchHooks::preprocessStatusMessages() runs on hook_preprocess_status_messages() and hands $variables['message_list'] to the error_squelch.message_squelcher service (Drupal\error_squelch\MessageSquelcher::filter()), which removes any status/warning/error whose text matches a configured pattern before the status-messages template renders. Matching is case-insensitive substring by default, or PHP regex (including delimiters) when the use_regex option is on; invalid regexes are skipped silently.

Key features: an admin settings form at /admin/config/development/error-squelch (config object error_squelch.settings); an optional log_suppressed toggle that records each suppressed message to the error_squelch log channel for an audit trail; a test_mode toggle that injects a known status message visible only to holders of the 'administer error squelch' permission so operators can confirm the filter works; and Drush commands error-squelch:list / add / remove (aliases esl / esa / esrm) for CLI pattern management. Uses modern Drupal patterns: #[Hook] OO hooks with a #[LegacyHook] procedural wrapper for core 10.3-11.0, and #config_target throughout the form.

Requirements: Drupal 10.3 or later, or Drupal 11; no additional modules; Drush 11 or later only for the optional CLI commands.
